comments.author: MelvinBot
comments.text:
## Proposal ### Please re-state the problem that we are trying to solve in this issue. After you split an expense and delete both splits, the remaining expense still shows "1 of 2" arrows. The arrow opens a "Hmm... it's not here" page. I reproduced this on web: ### What is the root cause of that problem? The arrow list still holds the original expense from before the split. 1. When you open expense B, the app saves the report's expense IDs `[A, B]` as the list the arrows use. 2. Splitting B doesn't remove B from Onyx. It moves B to the hidden split report `-2` ([`SplitTransactionUpdate.ts:1706-1715`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/ef784ba78226f211bbaa5d6698a5a162c20221e9/src/libs/actions/IOU/SplitTransactionUpdate.ts#L1706-L1715)). 3. [`useCarouselTransactionIDs.ts:43`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/ef784ba78226f211bbaa5d6698a5a162c20221e9/src/hooks/useCarouselTransactionIDs.ts#L43) only drops expenses that are deleted or pending delete. B is neither, so it stays in the list. 4. The splits were never in the list, so deleting them changes nothing. The list stays `[A, B]`, which shows "1 of 2". The arrow then opens B on report `-2`. In my repro the arrow went to `/e/-2`, which doesn't exist. ### What changes do you think we should make in order to solve the problem? 1. In `useCarouselTransactionIDs`, also filter out split originals. Use the existing helper [`isSplitContainerTransaction`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/ef784ba78226f211bbaa5d6698a5a162c20221e9/src/libs/TransactionUtils/index.ts#L1475-L1477), which checks for `reportID === SPLIT_REPORT_ID`. The original should never be a navigation target, even while its splits still exist. Both `MoneyReportHeader` and `MoneyRequestHeader` use this hook, so both hide the arrows. 2. Add a unit test. Seed `[A, B]`, set B's `reportID` to `-2`, and check that the hook returns `[A]`. ### What alternative solutions did you explore? (Optional) In the split flow, also remove the original's ID from the saved list using `removeActiveTransactionIDsForReport`. [Remove moved expenses from their old report's prev/next carousel](https://github.com/Expensify/App/pull/103998) does the same thing for moved expenses. This works alongside the filter fix but doesn't replace it, because other flows could restore a stale list.
Investigation details - The arrows render from [`MoneyReportHeader.tsx:104-108`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/ef784ba78226f211bbaa5d6698a5a162c20221e9/src/components/MoneyReportHeader.tsx#L104-L108) and [`MoneyRequestHeader.tsx:197-203`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/ef784ba78226f211bbaa5d6698a5a162c20221e9/src/components/MoneyRequestHeader.tsx#L197-L203). The counter is in [`MoneyRequestReportTransactionsNavigation.tsx:435-451`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/ef784ba78226f211bbaa5d6698a5a162c20221e9/src/components/MoneyRequestReportView/MoneyRequestReportTransactionsNavigation.tsx#L435-L451). - The list is saved from the report's visible IDs in [`MoneyRequestReportTransactionList.tsx:264-274`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/ef784ba78226f211bbaa5d6698a5a162c20221e9/src/components/MoneyRequestReportView/MoneyRequestReportTransactionList.tsx#L264-L274). - The report view refreshes the list only on the Search report screen ([`useMoneyRequestReportActiveTransactionIDs.ts:20-23`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/ef784ba78226f211bbaa5d6698a5a162c20221e9/src/components/MoneyRequestReportView/useMoneyRequestReportActiveTransactionIDs.ts#L20-L23)), so the list stays stale when you open the report from the workspace chat. - The arrow stays enabled because `canResolveSibling` only rejects expenses on report `0`, not `-2` ([`MoneyRequestReportTransactionsNavigation.tsx:322-344`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/ef784ba78226f211bbaa5d6698a5a162c20221e9/src/components/MoneyRequestReportView/MoneyRequestReportTransactionsNavigation.tsx#L322-L344)). - Web repro: the report showed 3 rows after the split and 1 row after deleting both splits. The counter read "1 of 2", and the arrow opened the not-found page: **Possibly related:** [Expense - Split can be opened after deleting offline and it opens not here page](https://github.com/Expensify/App/issues/103791)
--- **Next Steps for Contributor+ team:** **To accept:** `@MelvinBot implement [this](https://github.com/Expensify/App/issues/104307)` to create a draft PR. **To refine:** `@MelvinBot ` **To reject:** Explain why you are rejecting Melvin's proposal. --- _[view run](https://github.com/Expensify/melvin/actions/runs/39090243502)_ · _[view recording](https://melvinbot-assets.exops.io/session-39090243502-1-1aa08877-64dc-438a-8c21-d1f6e3e55695.webm)_

comments.author: camesenin
comments.text:
## Proposal

### Please re-state the problem that we are trying to solve in this issue.
After splitting an expense and deleting both split items, the remaining expense still displays the carousel arrow navigation showing "1 of 2". Clicking the navigation arrow opens the "It's not here" error page.

### What is the root cause of that problem?
1. In `src/hooks/useCarouselTransactionIDs.ts:43`, `validTransactionIDsSelector` checks:
```typescript
return !isTransactionPendingDelete(transaction) && !isDeletedTransaction(transaction);
```
2. When an expense is split (`SplitTransactionUpdate.ts:1706-1715`), the original container transaction is moved to `CONST.REPORT.SPLIT_REPORT_ID` (`-2`). It is neither marked as pending delete nor deleted.
3. Because the container transaction is not marked as deleted, it remains in `seededTransactionIDs`.
4. As a result, after both split children are deleted, the carousel still holds the remaining expense and the container expense, displaying "1 of 2". Clicking the arrow navigates to report `-2`, which does not exist.

### What changes do you think we should make in order to solve the problem?
1. In `src/hooks/useCarouselTransactionIDs.ts`, filter out split container transactions in `validTransactionIDsSelector`:
```typescript
return !isTransactionPendingDelete(transaction) && !isDeletedTransaction(transaction) && !isSplitContainerTransaction(transaction);
```
Import `isSplitContainerTransaction` from `@libs/TransactionUtils`.
2. In `src/components/MoneyRequestReportView/MoneyRequestReportTransactionsNavigation.tsx:343` (`canResolveSibling`), guard against `siblingTransaction.reportID === CONST.REPORT.SPLIT_REPORT_ID`.
3. Add a unit test verifying `useCarouselTransactionIDs` excludes transactions assigned to `SPLIT_REPORT_ID`.

comments.author: taieddie
comments.text:
## Proposal

### Please re-state the problem that we are trying to solve in this issue.
Arrow navigation ("1 of 2") remains visible in a report header and navigates to an "It's not here" screen even when only one valid expense remains after deleting split expenses.

### What is the root cause of that problem?
When an expense is split into child expenses, its original container transaction is moved to `CONST.REPORT.SPLIT_REPORT_ID` (`-2`) in `src/libs/actions/IOU/SplitTransactionUpdate.ts` (lines 1706-1715).

In `src/hooks/useCarouselTransactionIDs.ts` (line 43), `validTransactionIDsSelector` only filters out expenses that are pending delete or deleted:
`return !isTransactionPendingDelete(transaction) && !isDeletedTransaction(transaction);`
Because the original container transaction is neither marked deleted nor pending delete, it remains in `validTransactionIDs`. The container transaction never leaves.

When both created split expenses are deleted, only the single remaining non-split expense exists on the report. However, `useCarouselTransactionIDs` continues returning both the remaining expense and the container transaction (length of 2). Because of this, `MoneyReportHeader.tsx` (line 108) evaluates `activeTransactionIDs.length > 1` as true, showing the "1 of 2" arrow navigation.

Clicking the navigation arrow invokes `navigateToSibling` in `MoneyRequestReportTransactionsNavigation.tsx`. In `canResolveSibling` (lines 322-344) and `resolveSiblingReportID` (lines 258-312), the logic only guards against `CONST.REPORT.UNREPORTED_REPORT_ID` (`0`), not `CONST.REPORT.SPLIT_REPORT_ID` (`-2`). The app attempts to navigate to target report ID `-2`. Because report `-2` does not exist, the user lands on the "It's not here" page.

### What changes do you think we should make in order to solve the problem?
1. In `src/hooks/useCarouselTransactionIDs.ts`, update `validTransactionIDsSelector` to filter out split container transactions:
`return !isTransactionPendingDelete(transaction) && !isDeletedTransaction(transaction) && !isSplitContainerTransaction(transaction);`
Import `isSplitContainerTransaction` from `@libs/TransactionUtils`. This reactively drops the split container from the carousel as soon as `reportID` updates to `-2`.

2. In `src/components/MoneyRequestReportView/MoneyRequestReportTransactionsNavigation.tsx`:
   - In `canResolveSibling` (line 327), add an early return of `false` if `siblingTransaction?.reportID === CONST.REPORT.SPLIT_REPORT_ID`. This check must sit right at the start of the function, before checking descriptors or `siblingParentReportAction?.childReportID`, ensuring a split container never resolves as an openable sibling.
   - In `resolveSiblingReportID` (line 265), add an early return of `undefined` if `siblingTransaction?.reportID === CONST.REPORT.SPLIT_REPORT_ID`.

3. Add unit test coverage in `tests/unit/hooks/useCarouselTransactionIDsTest.ts` verifying that `useCarouselTransactionIDs` excludes transactions assigned to `SPLIT_REPORT_ID`. In `tests/unit/components/MoneyRequestReportTransactionsNavigationTest.tsx`, verify that `canResolveSibling` and `resolveSiblingReportID` reject siblings with `reportID === SPLIT_REPORT_ID` even when a descriptor or report action exists.

### What alternative solutions did you explore? (Optional)
Earlier proposals by @MelvinBot and @camesenin only proposed adding `!isSplitContainerTransaction(transaction)` to `useCarouselTransactionIDs.ts` and placing a guard at the end of `canResolveSibling`.

Their fatal flaw is that adding the check only at line 343 in `canResolveSibling` misses the earlier returns for descriptors and child report actions on lines 330-333. If an action or descriptor exists for the sibling, `canResolveSibling` returns true before line 343, keeping the arrow clickable. Placing the guard at the top of both `canResolveSibling` and `resolveSiblingReportID` guarantees that report `-2` is rejected before any descriptor or action resolution runs.

comments.author: zackthompson317
comments.text:
## Proposal

### Please re-state the problem that we are trying to solve in this issue.
After splitting an expense and then deleting both splits, the report is left with one expense, but the header still shows "1 of 2" arrows, and the arrow opens the "It's not here" page.

### What is the root cause of that problem?
The prev/next carousel is a global seed (`TRANSACTION_THREAD_NAVIGATION_TRANSACTION_IDS`) written when an expense row is opened, here `[A, B]` with source `reportRow:<reportID>`. The app's contract is that **whoever moves an expense off a report prunes it from that report's carousel**. `changeTransactionsReport` does this for every move via `removeMovedTransactionsFromCarousel` → `removeActiveTransactionIDsForReport` (added in #103998):

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/ef784ba78226f211bbaa5d6698a5a162c20221e9/src/libs/actions/Transaction.ts#L2144-L2152

Splitting is a move that skips that contract. `updateSplitTransactions` moves the original expense B to the hidden split report `-2` with a direct Onyx `SET`, and never touches the carousel:

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/ef784ba78226f211bbaa5d6698a5a162c20221e9/src/libs/actions/IOU/SplitTransactionUpdate.ts#L1706-L1715

So the seed keeps `[A, B]` even though B is no longer on the report. Deleting the two splits doesn't change it (they were never in the seed). Once A is the only expense, `MoneyReportHeader` anchors on it, sees two IDs, and shows "1 of 2". The arrow then resolves B to report `-2`.

The earlier proposals filter B out inside `useCarouselTransactionIDs` (line 43). That hides the header arrows, but the stale seed is still in Onyx and in the module state, and **not every consumer goes through that hook**. `OneTransactionThreadRedirectHandler` reads the raw key and treats any seed longer than 1 as "the user is stepping through expenses":

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/ef784ba78226f211bbaa5d6698a5a162c20221e9/src/pages/inbox/OneTransactionThreadRedirectHandler.tsx#L30-L32
https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/ef784ba78226f211bbaa5d6698a5a162c20221e9/src/pages/inbox/OneTransactionThreadRedirectHandler.tsx#L83-L91

With the stale `[A, B]`, that check stays `true` for A's thread even though A is now the only expense on its report, so the normal one-transaction redirect to the parent report is suppressed. A hook-only filter fixes the arrows but leaves this second symptom of the same stale seed.

### What changes do you think we should make in order to solve the problem?
1. **Fix it where the move happens.** In `updateSplitTransactions`, in the non-reverse branch right after `writeSplit(...)` (`SplitTransactionUpdate.ts` ~L2158-L2174), prune the original from its old report's carousel using the existing helper, the same way `changeTransactionsReport` does:
```ts
// Splitting moves the original to SPLIT_REPORT_ID, so it must leave the carousel seeded from its old report,
// just like a regular move (see removeMovedTransactionsFromCarousel).
if (isCreationOfSplits && originalTransaction?.reportID && originalTransaction.reportID !== CONST.REPORT.SPLIT_REPORT_ID) {
    removeActiveTransactionIDsForReport([originalTransactionID], originalTransaction.reportID);
}
```
`removeActiveTransactionIDsForReport` already only acts when the carousel is owned by that report (`report:`/`reportRow:`/`reportPreview:` sources), leaves search carousels alone, and clears the carousel when fewer than 2 IDs remain. So it can't break the arrows on Search. If the user is in the split-expenses flow, the call can go inside the existing `TransitionTracker.runAfterTransitions` callback next to `removeDraftSplitTransaction` so it doesn't re-render mid-transition.

2. **Defense in depth (optional, agreeing with earlier proposals):** also return `false` for `isSplitContainerTransaction(transaction)` in `validTransactionIDsSelector`, and have `canResolveSibling` reject `CONST.REPORT.SPLIT_REPORT_ID` the same way it rejects `UNREPORTED_REPORT_ID` (L343). This covers a seed that was restored from somewhere else, but on its own it doesn't fix the raw-key consumer above.

3. **Tests:**
   - In `tests/unit/libs/actions/TransactionThreadNavigationTest.ts`-style setup, seed `[A, B]` with source `reportRow:R`, call `updateSplitTransactions` creating splits from B, and assert the carousel no longer contains B (and is cleared, since only A remains).
   - Assert a carousel seeded from `search:<hash>` is left untouched by the split.
   - Assert `OneTransactionThreadRedirectHandler` redirects A's thread to the parent report after the splits are deleted.

### What alternative solutions did you explore? (Optional)
- Filtering only in `useCarouselTransactionIDs` (earlier proposals): fixes the header, but leaves the stale seed for `OneTransactionThreadRedirectHandler` and any future raw-key reader, and breaks the "writer prunes on move" pattern from #103998.
- Re-seeding from `useMoneyRequestReportActiveTransactionIDs` outside Search: rejected, because that hook is deliberately Search-only to avoid clobbering carousels owned by other screens.

comments.text:
## Proposal

### Please re-state the problem that we are trying to solve in this issue.

After splitting an expense and deleting both splits, the report is left with a single expense, but the report header still renders the "1 of 2" prev/next arrows, and tapping an arrow opens the "It’s not here" page.

### What is the root cause of that problem?

The prev/next carousel is seeded when an expense row is opened, stored under ONYXKEYS.TRANSACTION_THREAD_NAVIGATION_TRANSACTION_IDS. The codebase has an established contract: whoever moves an expense off a report prunes it from that report's carousel, implemented by removeActiveTransactionIDsForReport and enforced for every move through changeTransactionsReport (added in PR #103998).

Splitting breaks that contract. The split action moves the original expense to the hidden split report (CONST.REPORT.SPLIT_REPORT_ID) but never prunes the carousel seeded from the old report, so the seed keeps the original's ID even though the report no longer shows it. Deleting the two splits changes nothing, because the splits were never in the seed. With one expense left on the report, the header anchors on it, sees two IDs in the seed, and renders "1 of 2" arrows; the arrow then resolves the stale ID to an expense that no longer belongs to a visible report, landing on "It’s not here".

### What changes do you think we should make in order to solve the problem?

Fix it where the move happens, not in the consumers:

1. In the split action, in the non-reverse branch right after the original expense is moved to SPLIT_REPORT_ID, prune it from its old report's carousel with the existing helper, exactly like changeTransactionsReport does: removeActiveTransactionIDsForReport([originalTransactionID], originalTransaction.reportID); This helper only acts when the carousel is owned by that report and clears the carousel when fewer than 2 IDs remain, so it cannot break search-seeded carousels or other screens.
2. Tests in tests/unit/libs/actions/TransactionThreadNavigationTest.ts-style setup: seed the carousel with [A, B] from a report, perform a split on B, and assert B is pruned and the carousel is cleared; assert a search-seeded carousel is untouched; assert the header shows no arrows with a single expense.
3. Manual verification of the exact repro steps: split an expense, delete both splits, confirm no arrows render and no "It’s not here" navigation is possible.

### What alternative solutions did you explore? (Optional)

- Filtering the stale ID inside the carousel-reading hook: fixes the header arrows but leaves the stale seed in Onyx for every other consumer of the raw key, and breaks the "writer prunes on move" pattern the codebase already established in PR #103998.

## Proposal

### Please re-state the problem that we are trying to solve in this issue.
After splitting an expense on a report with two expenses and deleting the resulting split children, the report is left with a single expense, but the prev/next arrow navigation still displays "1 of 2" and clicking an arrow navigates to the "It's not here" page.

### What is the root cause of that problem?
There are two reinforcing defects in the carousel lifecycle when splitting expenses:

1. **Seed Pruning on Move (Writer Lifecycle):**
   - When an expense is moved to another report, `changeTransactionsReport` in `src/libs/actions/Transaction.ts` (lines 2148–2151) calls `removeActiveTransactionIDsForReport(transactionIDs, oldReportID)` to prune moved expenses from carousels seeded from that report.
   - However, when splitting an expense in `src/libs/actions/IOU/Split.ts`, the original expense is moved to `CONST.REPORT.SPLIT_REPORT_ID` (`-2`), but `removeActiveTransactionIDsForReport` is never called. The stale transaction ID remains in `ONYXKEYS.TRANSACTION_THREAD_NAVIGATION_TRANSACTION_IDS`.

2. **Consumer Filtering (`useCarouselTransactionIDs`):**
   - In `src/hooks/useCarouselTransactionIDs.ts` (lines 35–40):
     ```ts
     return !isTransactionPendingDelete(transaction) && !isDeletedTransaction(transaction);
     ```
   - When an expense is split into children, the parent container transaction has `transaction.reportID = CONST.REPORT.SPLIT_REPORT_ID`. It is neither pending delete nor deleted, so `useCarouselTransactionIDs` continues to treat it as an active sibling in the carousel.
   - When the two splits are deleted, the report only has one remaining expense, but the carousel retains both IDs (the remaining expense + the split container transaction), rendering the "1 of 2" arrows and navigating to "It's not here" when clicked.

### What changes do you think we should make in order to solve the problem?

We should resolve both the writer lifecycle and the consumer selector to ensure total robustness:

1. **Prune Moved Transaction in Split Action (`Split.ts`):**
   In `src/libs/actions/IOU/Split.ts`, right where the original transaction is moved to `CONST.REPORT.SPLIT_REPORT_ID`, call `removeActiveTransactionIDsForReport([originalTransactionID], originalTransaction.reportID)`. This automatically prunes the ID and clears the carousel if fewer than 2 expenses remain, matching the contract established in PR #103998.

2. **Defensive Filter in `useCarouselTransactionIDs.ts`:**
   In `src/hooks/useCarouselTransactionIDs.ts`, import `isSplitContainerTransaction` from `@libs/TransactionUtils` and include it in the `validTransactionIDsSelector` filter:
   ```diff
   --- a/src/hooks/useCarouselTransactionIDs.ts
   +++ b/src/hooks/useCarouselTransactionIDs.ts
   @@ -1,4 +1,4 @@
   -import {isDeletedTransaction, isTransactionPendingDelete} from '@libs/TransactionUtils';
   +import {isDeletedTransaction, isSplitContainerTransaction, isTransactionPendingDelete} from '@libs/TransactionUtils';
    
    import ONYXKEYS from '@src/ONYXKEYS';
    import type * as OnyxTypes from '@src/types/onyx';
   @@ -37,7 +37,7 @@ function useCarouselTransactionIDs(): CarouselTransactionIDs {
                if (!transaction) {
                    return !!siblingDescriptors?.[transactionID];
                }
   -            return !isTransactionPendingDelete(transaction) && !isDeletedTransaction(transaction);
   +            return !isTransactionPendingDelete(transaction) && !isDeletedTransaction(transaction) && !isSplitContainerTransaction(transaction);
            });
   ```

3. **Navigation Guard in `MoneyRequestReportTransactionsNavigation.tsx`:**
   Ensure `canResolveSibling` and `resolveSiblingReportID` verify `!isSplitContainerTransaction(siblingTransaction)` so orphaned container transactions can never trigger invalid route transitions.

### What alternative solutions did you explore? (Optional)
- Filtering only in the consumer hook (`useCarouselTransactionIDs`): While this hides the header arrows, it leaves the stale ID in Onyx seed keys for `OneTransactionThreadRedirectHandler` and breaks the established "writer prunes on move" invariant from PR #103998.
- Relying only on writer pruning: Combining writer pruning with consumer filtering provides defense-in-depth across asynchronous Onyx batches and cached snapshots.

## Proposal

### Please re-state the problem that we are trying to solve in this issue.
After splitting an expense on a report with two expenses and deleting the resulting split children, the report is left with a single expense, but the prev/next arrow navigation still displays "1 of 2" and clicking an arrow navigates to the "It's not here" page.

### What is the root cause of that problem?
There are two distinct root causes causing this inconsistency across the carousel lifecycle:

1. **Writer Invariant Violation (`Split.ts`):**
   - In `src/libs/actions/IOU/Split.ts`, when an expense is split into child expenses, the original transaction is moved to `CONST.REPORT.SPLIT_REPORT_ID` (`-2`).
   - However, unlike `changeTransactionsReport` in `src/libs/actions/Transaction.ts` which explicitly calls `removeActiveTransactionIDsForReport(transactionIDs, oldReportID)` upon moving expenses, `Split.ts` never cleans up the moved transaction from the report's carousel seed key (`ONYXKEYS.TRANSACTION_THREAD_NAVIGATION_TRANSACTION_IDS`).

2. **Consumer Selector Oversight (`useCarouselTransactionIDs.ts`):**
   - In `src/hooks/useCarouselTransactionIDs.ts` (lines 35-40), the selector only checks:
     ```ts
     return !isTransactionPendingDelete(transaction) && !isDeletedTransaction(transaction);
     ```
   - When an expense is split, the container transaction has `transaction.reportID = CONST.REPORT.SPLIT_REPORT_ID`. Because it is neither pending delete nor deleted, `useCarouselTransactionIDs` continues to treat it as an active sibling in the carousel.
   - When the two splits are deleted, the report only has one remaining expense, but the carousel still includes both the remaining expense and the split container transaction, improperly rendering the "1 of 2" navigation arrows.

### What changes do you think we should make in order to solve the problem?

1. **Prune Moved Transaction in Split Action (`src/libs/actions/IOU/Split.ts`):**
   Right when the original transaction is moved to `CONST.REPORT.SPLIT_REPORT_ID`, invoke:
   ```ts
   removeActiveTransactionIDsForReport([originalTransactionID], originalTransaction.reportID);
   ```
   This ensures that the writer immediately maintains the carousel invariant established in PR #103998.

2. **Add Defensive Filter to Consumer Selector (`src/hooks/useCarouselTransactionIDs.ts`):**
   Import `isSplitContainerTransaction` from `@libs/TransactionUtils` and include it in the `validTransactionIDsSelector`:
   ```diff
   - return !isTransactionPendingDelete(transaction) && !isDeletedTransaction(transaction);
   + return !isTransactionPendingDelete(transaction) && !isDeletedTransaction(transaction) && !isSplitContainerTransaction(transaction);
   ```

3. **Navigation Guards in `src/components/MoneyRequestReportTransactionsNavigation.tsx`:**
   In `canResolveSibling` and `resolveSiblingReportID`, verify `!isSplitContainerTransaction(siblingTransaction)` so orphaned container transactions can never trigger invalid route transitions.

4. **Automated Unit Tests:**
   Add unit test in `tests/unit/useCarouselTransactionIDsTest.ts` validating that when a split parent container transaction is present, it is excluded from active carousel IDs and navigation controls remain hidden when $\le 1$ valid expense exists.

### What alternative solutions did you explore? (Optional)
- *Filtering only in `useCarouselTransactionIDs`:* While this hides the header arrows, it leaves the stale ID in Onyx seed keys for `OneTransactionThreadRedirectHandler` and violates the writer-pruning contract from PR #103998.
- *Writer-only pruning:* Does not defend against cached snapshots or asynchronous Onyx batch re-render cycles. Combining writer pruning with consumer filtering provides complete defense-in-depth.

### What is the root cause of that problem?
There are two interrelated root causes in the carousel navigation lifecycle:

1. **Seed Pruning on Move (Writer Contract Violation):**
   - In PR #103998, a contract was established where moving an expense off a report prunes it from the report's carousel seed (`ONYXKEYS.TRANSACTION_THREAD_NAVIGATION_TRANSACTION_IDS`) via `removeActiveTransactionIDsForReport`.
   - However, in `src/libs/actions/IOU/SplitTransactionUpdate.ts` (lines 1706–1715), splitting an expense moves the original container transaction to the hidden split report (`CONST.REPORT.SPLIT_REPORT_ID` / `-2`), but never calls `removeActiveTransactionIDsForReport`.
   - As a result, the original transaction ID remains in the carousel seed even though it is no longer visible on the report. Deleting the two splits changes nothing because the splits were never in the seed. When the remaining expense is viewed, the carousel still holds 2 IDs, rendering "1 of 2" arrows. Clicking the arrow tries to navigate to report `-2`, which lands on "It's not here".

2. **Consumer Selector Oversight (`useCarouselTransactionIDs.ts`):**
   - In `src/hooks/useCarouselTransactionIDs.ts` (line 43), `validTransactionIDsSelector` only filters out expenses that are pending delete or deleted:
     `return !isTransactionPendingDelete(transaction) && !isDeletedTransaction(transaction);`
   - Split container transactions have `reportID === CONST.REPORT.SPLIT_REPORT_ID`. They are neither pending delete nor deleted, so `useCarouselTransactionIDs` continues treating them as active siblings.

### What changes do you think we should make in order to solve the problem?
We should apply a defense-in-depth fix addressing both the writer move action and the consumer selector:

1. **Prune on Split Move (`SplitTransactionUpdate.ts`):**
   In `src/libs/actions/IOU/SplitTransactionUpdate.ts`, in `updateSplitTransactions` right after the original transaction is moved to `CONST.REPORT.SPLIT_REPORT_ID`, prune it from the report's active carousel:
   ```typescript
   if (isCreationOfSplits && originalTransaction?.reportID && originalTransaction.reportID !== CONST.REPORT.SPLIT_REPORT_ID) {
       removeActiveTransactionIDsForReport([originalTransactionID], originalTransaction.reportID);
   }
   ```
   This automatically maintains the writer-pruning contract from PR #103998 and clears the carousel if only 1 expense remains.

2. **Consumer Filtering (`useCarouselTransactionIDs.ts`):**
